sources.title: Ward Whitt, Continuous-Time Markov Chains (full lecture notes, 2006)
sources.locator: §2 Lemma 2.1 and §§3.1–3.4, especially Theorems 3.1, 3.2 and 3.4; PDF pp. 2–16. Row-vector formulas are transposed to the declared column convention.

read_evidence.method: Fetched the complete 40-page PDF and extracted its text; inspected the full Chapman–Kolmogorov argument, finite-state rate and forward-equation development, matrix-exponential proof, and uniformization construction at these locators.

contents.name: Lemma 2.1: Chapman–Kolmogorov equations for homogeneous CTMC transition probabilities
contents.support: The given-chain definition records the transition-kernel semigroup convention and names its composition explicitly; the proof does not reconstruct a countable chain from rates.

contents.name: Theorem 3.1: Kolmogorov forward and backward differential equations
contents.support: The local finite-dimensional master-equation proof establishes the forward equation in the column convention and uniqueness.

contents.name: Theorem 3.2 and its full proof: finite matrix-exponential representation
contents.support: The matrix series, termwise derivative and finite generator solution are proved locally, including the convergence and commuting-product steps.

contents.name: Theorem 3.3: removal of transitions from a state back to itself
contents.reason: The carriers define rates only between distinct states and do not model marked self-events; this theorem does not supply a premise used by the finite generator, uniformization, or killed-projection arguments.

contents.name: Theorem 3.4 and §3.4 equations (3.24)–(3.30): validity and Poisson representation of uniformization
contents.support: Its Poisson mixture is transposed to the explicit column convention and proved from the local matrix-series and scalar Poisson suppliers.

sources.title: Brian Munsky and Mustafa Khammash, The Finite State Projection Algorithm for the Solution of the Chemical Master Equation (Journal of Chemical Physics 124, 044104, 2006)
sources.locator: §II equations (2.3)–(2.8), Theorems 2.1–2.2, and §III, printed pp. 044104-2–044104-6; proofs of both finite-state projection theorems inspected.

read_evidence.method: Fetched and extracted the complete 13-page article; read the full mathematical background, complete proofs of Theorems 2.1 and 2.2, the finite projection algorithm, and Proposition 3.1 at the printed locators.

contents.name: Equations (2.3)–(2.6): countable reaction state space, transition-rate matrix, and chemical master equation
contents.support: The source fixes the master-equation matrix context; the local definition states the distinct-state column-rate convention and proves its uses locally.

contents.name: Theorem 2.1: finite principal projection is componentwise below the full solution
contents.locator: §II, Theorem 2.1 and complete proof, printed pp. 044104-3–044104-4
contents.support: The local proof obtains the componentwise inequality by the common-path first-exit event for a given nonexplosive chain.

contents.name: Theorem 2.2: exact projection missing-mass error certificate
contents.locator: §II, Theorem 2.2 and complete proof, printed pp. 044104-4–044104-5
contents.support: The local result proves the embedded l1 error equals cemetery mass and adds the bounded-observable oscillation bound.

contents.name: §III finite-state projection algorithm: enlarge a finite state set using the computed lost-mass criterion
contents.support: The local algorithm checks a supplied nested finite list, records a certified interval at every attempted projection, and returns inconclusive when its finite budget is insufficient.

contents.name: Proposition 3.1: finite stopping when an adequate finite projection exists
contents.reason: This pair proves termination only for its supplied finite candidate list and makes no existence claim for a projection meeting every tolerance, as required by the controlling owner direction.

sources.title: Bennett L. Fox and Peter W. Glynn, Computing Poisson Probabilities (Communications of the ACM 31(4), 1988)
sources.locator: §§1–6, printed pp. 440–445; Proposition 1, Poisson-tail bounds, positive recurrences, numerical-stability discussion, and the complete proofs of Propositions 5–6 inspected.

read_evidence.method: Fetched the complete article PDF and extracted its full text; read the complete truncation-error argument, algorithm and stability discussion, tail-bound propositions, and proofs of Propositions 5–6.

contents.name: Proposition 1: rigorous error bound for a Poisson-truncated bounded-reward calculation
contents.support: The paper motivates certified omitted-mass control; the local theorem independently proves the exact one-sided Poisson-tail identity and the time-split arithmetic-error ledger.

contents.name: §1.2 and §2: positive recursive Poisson weights and numerical-stability analysis
contents.support: The local procedure uses a positive forward weight recurrence after splitting to substep parameter at most one, and refuses an uncertified rounded tail.

contents.name: §3: finite search for truncation points and underflow checks
contents.support: The local procedure searches a finite term-cap list and reports budget exhaustion; it does not import the source’s mode-centered truncation-point routine.

contents.name: Propositions 2–3 and Corollaries 1–2: rigorous Poisson right- and left-tail bounds
contents.support: The carriers prove a separate simple geometric right-tail majorant directly from the exact Poisson mass ratio and use it as the certificate.

contents.name: Proposition 4: normal-tail integral bound used to derive the source’s mode-centered tail bounds
contents.reason: The local certificate uses an exact Poisson mass recurrence and a geometric series; no normal-tail approximation, error function, or mode-centered estimate enters any claim.

contents.name: Propositions 5–6 and Corollaries 3–4: lower bounds on individual Poisson masses for underflow prevention
contents.reason: The local method time-splits and requires a separately certified arithmetic error; it does not rescale mode-centered weights or claim Fox–Glynn underflow guarantees.

contents.name: Complete proofs of Propositions 5–6
contents.reason: These proofs support underflow lower bounds that the assigned algorithm does not use; its tail, recurrence, and error claims have complete local arguments.
